name: Tallán
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Extinct; only colonial wordlists (Ramos Cabredo 1950; Zevallos Quinones 1948), no phonological description

sources.citation: Urban, Matthias. 2019. Lost Languages of the Peruvian North Coast. Estudios Indiana 12. Berlin: Ibero-Amerikanisches Institut / Gebr. Mann. 314 pp. (open access)
sources.note: Ch. IV 'The Tallan languages' pp. 73-96, 'Sound system' pp. 86-92: treats the tilde, Colan/Catacaos correspondences, voiced stops, mid vowels, high-vowel alternation, phonotactics and root structure; there is NO stress subsection and no word-stress rule is stated (unlike the Mochica and Quingnam chapters, which each have one). Only stress-adjacent remarks: p. 90 the recurrent surname ending -qué bears a stressed é ('As the syllable is stress-bearing, it is very unlikely that its vowel is paragogic'); p. 85 surname endings -qué, -lupú, -valú are cited with final acute; Appendix A pp. 277-280 s…
